newsitem.title: USA: Crucial Korea meeting opens on positive note.
newsitem.headline: Crucial Korea meeting opens on positive note.

text.p: North Korea went into a crucial meeting on Korean peninsula peace efforts on Wednesday on a positive note, suggesting it would produce "good results."
"I think we will come out with good results," Kim Gye Gwan, Pyongyang's delegation chief, told his South Korean counterpart during a photo session with journalists.
South Korea's chief negotiator, Song Young Shik, was also in an upbeat mood, laughing and chatting with Kim. He said he hoped the meeting would reflect the warm spring day in New York.

The meeting between U.S., North Korean and South Korean officials was called to determine whether Stalinist North Korea, threatened by famine, is prepared to make a serious stab at peace with democratic South Korea.

U.S. officials have been cautiously optimistic that Pyongyang will respond positively to Washington's year-old joint proposal with South Korea for four-party peace talks -- also including China -- that would finally close the books on the 1950-53 Korean War.
Asked by reporters Wednesday how he thought the meeting would go, South Korea's Song held up his fingers crossed, a sign that he hoped the results would be positive.
